Maine Department of Labor announces October workplace safety and labor law training schedule

September 24, 2026

For Immediate Release: Thursday, Sept. 24, 2026

Media Contact: Autumn Mahoney, Communications Specialist media.dol@maine.gov

AUGUSTA - The Maine Department of Labor offers free workplace safety and labor law training to help employers, managers, supervisors, human resources professionals and others understand workplace safety requirements and Maine labor laws. The Department has announced its schedule of October classes, with trainings offered through SafetyWorks! and the Bureau of Labor Standards.

Registration is required, and space may be limited. View the October schedule and register for a class.

Unless otherwise noted, classes are held at the SafetyWorks! Training Institute at the Maine Department of Labor, 45 Commerce Drive in Augusta.

October Class Schedule

Fire Extinguisher/Emergency Action Plans/Workplace Violence Thursday, Oct. 1, 8:30 a.m. to 3:30 p.m.
SafetyWorks! Training Institute, Augusta

Workplace emergencies include fire, medical, and workplace violence. This course covers the requirements of an emergency action plan, fire extinguisher use, and considering the potential for workplace violence. The SWTI Lab includes a fire extinguisher discharge activity to assist participants in learning how to use a fire extinguisher.

Bloodborne Pathogens Train-the-Trainer Friday, Oct. 2, 8:30 a.m. to 12:30 p.m. SafetyWorks! Training Institute, Augusta

This half-day class provides guidance on what is needed to be compliant with the bloodborne pathogen standard. This course will review written program requirements, training, documentation, Hepatitis B, and sharp logs.

Safety & Health Management Systems Tuesday, Oct. 6, 8:30 a.m. to 4 p.m. SafetyWorks! Training Institute, Augusta

Successful safety and health programs are more than just compliance with the OSHA standards. Injuries and illnesses are reduced when employers possess common elements to identify and address safety and health hazards. This course outlines roles and responsibilities, common principles, required functions and programs of a successful safety and health management system. This course prepares organizations who would like to pursue SHARP/ SHAPE.

Cold & Heat Illness Prevention Friday, Oct. 9, 8:30 a.m. to 12:30 p.m.
SafetyWorks! Training Institute, Augusta

Whether your employees work outside or inside, cold and hot temperatures can be hazardous to their health. This class covers cold and heat temperature illnesses, signs and symptoms, and control measures to prevent and treat temperature related injuries.

Welding/Compressed Gas Tuesday, Oct. 13, 8:30 a.m. to 12:30 p.m.
SafetyWorks! Training Institute, Augusta

This class covers the requirements of the welding standard, in addition to the storage and proper use of compressed gas. Proper inspection techniques of hoses, torches, and regulators will be demonstrated.

Wage & Hour Compliance Wednesday, Oct. 14, 9 a.m. to noon Maine Department of Health & Human Services, 200 Main St, Conference Room A, Lewiston

This course is designed for human resource or benefits professionals, accountants, business owners, managers, or payroll supervisors. Labor laws can be complex. ESTATE OF PUNG v. ISABELLA COUNTY, 
MICHIGAN 
certiorari to the united states court of appeals for 
the sixth circuit 
No. 25–95. Argued February 25, 2026—Decided June 23, 2026 
The Pung family owed $2,241.93 in real-property taxes, so local tax author-
ities in Isabella County, Michigan, initiated foreclosure proceedings and 
sold the Pung home—which was assessed at $194,400 for tax purposes— 
for $76,008 at public auction. Michael Pung sued in Federal court, and 
the District Court granted Pung partial summary judgment on his Fifth 
Amendment claim. The court held that Pung should receive only the 
surplus proceeds from the tax sale—i. e., the difference between the 
sale price and the tax debt—not the property's fair market value. The 
District Court also rejected Pung's claim under the Eighth Amendment 
Excessive Fines Clause. The Sixth Circuit affrmed. 
Held: 
1. The proper baseline for measuring “just compensation” following a 
tax sale is the auction sale price, not the property's hypothetical fair 
market value, at least when the sale is fairly conducted in light of the 
country's history of tax sales. Pp. 35–43. 
(a) For hundreds of years, English and American law have allowed 
the seizure and sale of property as a tax-collection method, provided 
that the government return any surplus proceeds to the debtor. Fed-
eral statutes from the early days of the Republic applied this rule,

Maine's Minimum Wage to Increase to $15.70 Per Hour in 2027

September 18, 2026

For Immediate Release: September 18, 2026

Media Contact: Autumn Mahoney, Communications Specialist media.dol@maine.gov

AUGUSTA - The Maine Department of Labor announced today that, effective January 1, 2027, the state minimum wage will increase from $15.10 to $15.70 per hour, based on data recently made available by the U.S. Department of Labor's Bureau of Labor Statistics. MDOL is required under Maine law (Maine statute Title 26, chapter 7, section 664) to make annual adjustments to the minimum wage based on the cost-of-living index (CPI-W) for the Northeast Region, after Maine voters amended the law by referendum in 2016. Between August 2025 and August 2026, there was a 4.1 percent increase in the CPI-W.

According to the U.S. Department of Labor's Bureau of Labor Statistics Current Population Survey for 2025, there were 28,000 hourly workers who were paid less than $15.00 per hour. These workers represent about four percent of all wage and salary workers (both paid at hourly rates and not paid at hourly rates) and about eight percent of wage and salary workers who are paid at hourly rates.

Agricultural workers in Maine are also entitled to the state minimum wage, after the Legislature enacted and Governor Mills signed "An Act to Establish a State Minimum Hourly Wage for Agricultural Workers" in 2025.

The "tip wage," or service employee minimum wage, will increase from $7.55 to $7.85 per hour. This means that service employees must receive a direct cash wage of at least $7.85 per hour from the employer. The employer must be able to show that the employee receives at least the minimum wage of $15.70 per hour when the direct wage and tips are combined at the end of the week. The amount of tips necessary to qualify as a service employee will increase from $191 to $199 per month.

The minimum salary threshold for exempting a worker from overtime pay must exceed 3,000 times the State's minimum wage or the annualized rate established by the U.S. Department of Labor, whichever is higher. Starting January 1, 2027, the new minimum salary threshold for salaried workers exempt from overtime will be $905.79 per week, or $47,101.08 per year. This is only one of the factors used in determining whether a worker is exempt from overtime pay under federal or state law. An individual can earn more than the minimum salary threshold and still be eligible for overtime. The duties of each worker must be considered as part of this analysis.

Employers can download the required minimum wage poster at no cost on the Department's website.

The minimum wage and overtime law can be found here.

More information about minimum wage and other labor standards is available on the Department's website

items.title: Digital Archives
items.content_text:
Welcome to the online digital collection of the Maine State Archives, a bureau within the Department of the Secretary of State. We maintain approximately 8 miles of official state records (both paper and digital) that are deemed permanently valuable. These records include bills introduced in the Legislature, reports from the Governor's Executive Council, election returns, deeds and maps from the Maine Land Office, vital statistics prior to 1892, federal census records up to 1880, county court records dating back to 1636, and military records through World War I, among others.
As of March 1, 2026, our online collection includes over one million individual records. The Maine State Archives will continue to expand this database as we digitize more of our collection. All documents are public records and are free to download. To begin your search, check the following sources:
Digital Archives Portal
: Open Access - online digital collection of the Maine State Archives.
ArchivesSpace Public Interface
: Use this database to search through the archival findings aids, collection structures, and descriptions of physical and digital records managed by the bureau.
Maine Memory Network
: A digital history platform featuring specific exhibits, historical photographs, and selected primary documents contributed by the Maine State Archives.
Family Search
: FamilySearch is the world’s largest free genealogy resource.

items.title: LGBTQ Veterans Day - September 20
items.content_text:
WHEREAS
, generations of lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, queer, and other LGBTQ veterans have served the United States with courage, professionalism, and distinction in every branch of the Armed Forces; and
WHEREAS
, LGBTQ servicemembers and veterans have contributed to the defense of the nation even during periods when military policy required many to conceal who they were or subjected them to discrimination, investigation, discharge, or unequal treatment; and
WHEREAS
, Maine is home to veterans, servicemembers, military families, public servants, and national security professionals whose service strengthens both the state and the nation; and
WHEREAS
, recognizing the service and sacrifice of LGBTQ veterans helps ensure that all who have worn the uniform are treated with dignity, receive the benefits and support they have earned, and remain connected to the communities they served; and
WHEREAS
, LGBTQ Veterans Day provides an opportunity to honor veterans living today, remember those who served before them, and recognize the continuing contributions of LGBTQ veterans to the civic life, security, and strength of Maine;
NOW, THEREFORE
, be it resolved that I, Janet T. Mills, Governor of the State of Maine, do hereby proclaim September 20, 2026 as
LGBTQ Veterans Day
throughout the State of Maine, and I encourage all Maine people to recognize the service, sacrifice, and contributions of LGBTQ veterans to our state and our nation.
In testimony whereof, I have caused
the Great Seal of the State to be
hereunto affixed GIVEN under my
hand at Augusta this second day
of September Two Thousand Twenty-Six

items.title: Updates to the National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System Definitions and Exclusions
items.content_text: The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) proposes to revise a regulatory definition under the Clean Water Act (CWA) permitting regulations pertaining to discharges in the contiguous zone and ocean. The proposal would revise the regulatory definition of "discharge of a pollutant" to reflect and faithfully implement the statutory exclusion of vessels and other floating craft that add pollutants in the contiguous zone or the ocean from inclusion in the definition of "discharge of a pollutant" or "discharge", and thus, from National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (NPDES) program requirements. The proposed rulemaking would also make conforming and clarifying changes to the NPDES regulatory exclusion for vessels and other floating craft. The effect of these changes would be that the addition of pollutants by a vessel or other floating craft in the contiguous zone or the ocean that is not secured to the seabed would not be a discharge and would not require CWA NPDES permit authorization to add pollutants to those waters.
